source_title_hint: El ejercicio definitivo para la movilidad de la cadera
primary_summary: This video explains the biomechanics of the 90/90 hip switch, highlighting common compensation patterns involving the spine and low back when individuals lack true hip mobility. It then provides detailed instructions on how to correctly perform the 90/90 position by focusing on specific points of contact for both the internally and externally rotated legs, aiming to maximize hip mobility gains and minimize compensation.

classification.usefulness_reason: The video provides detailed biomechanical explanations of hip joint movement during a common mobility drill, identifies common compensation patterns, and offers specific cues for correct execution. This is valuable for diagnostic support, explanation support, corrective exercise selection, and biomechanical concept retrieval.

problem_statements: Many people perform the 90/90 hip switch incorrectly.
Lack of genuine hip motion leads to compensation through the spine and low back.
Difficulty achieving true internal and external hip rotation in the 90/90 position.
habits_or_contexts: Performing hip mobility drills without understanding proper joint mechanics.
Compensating with spinal movement during hip rotation exercises.
key_visual_points: Animated anatomical model showing the 90/90 hip switch with highlighted leg angles.
Demonstration of incorrect 90/90 hip switch with spinal rotation and lifting of the back leg.
Demonstration of correct 90/90 hip switch with stable torso and proper leg positioning.
Skeleton model of the pelvis and femur demonstrating internal and external rotation.
Visual cues (arrows) indicating points of contact for the internally and externally rotated legs.
advice_mentioned: Focus on achieving genuine hip motion rather than compensating with the spine.
Identify and maintain specific points of contact for each leg in the 90/90 position.
Simply holding the correct 90/90 position with proper points of contact and breathing can restore hip mobility.
warnings_or_limitations: Avoid pinching or discomfort in the hips.
Do not turn your spine to force the legs into position; this indicates compensation.

knowledge_units.title: Complex Hip Joint Movement in 90/90 Hip Switch
knowledge_units.summary: The 90/90 hip switch involves complex movements where the femur constantly switches between internal and external rotation within the pelvis, and the pelvis also moves on the femur to accommodate these changes in motion. This requires significant mobility from both the hip joint and surrounding structures.
mechanisms: Femoral internal rotation on the back leg.
Femoral external rotation on the front leg.
Pelvic movement on the femur to accommodate changes in rotation and direction of motion.

knowledge_units.title: Spinal Compensation for Lack of Hip Mobility in 90/90 Hip Switch
knowledge_units.summary: When individuals lack the genuine hip mobility required for the 90/90 hip switch, they often compensate by moving and orienting through their spine and low back. This allows them to achieve the appearance of the position without truly engaging the hip joint's full range of motion.
observable_signs: Turning the spine in one direction to get the leg flat on the ground.
Re-orienting the low back to make up for limited hip movement.
mechanisms: Lack of genuine hip internal/external rotation.
Compensatory movement of the lumbar spine and pelvis.
errors_to_avoid: Turning your spine to help find the desired leg positions.

knowledge_units.title: Correct 90/90 Hip Switch - Internally Rotated Leg (Back Leg)
knowledge_units.summary: To achieve a genuine internally rotated position for the back leg in the 90/90 hip switch, focus on two specific points of contact: the inside knee and the inside ankle bone (medial malleolus). Both points should be in contact with the ground.
execution_steps: Ensure the inside of the knee of the back leg is in contact with the ground.
Ensure the inside ankle bone (medial malleolus) of the back leg is in contact with the ground.
cues: Find two points of contact: inside knee and inside ankle bone (medial malleolus).
This is a genuinely internally rotated leg, not just a position achieved by turning your spine.
errors_to_avoid: Turning your spine to force the leg flat on the ground.

knowledge_units.title: Correct 90/90 Hip Switch - Externally Rotated Leg (Front Leg)
knowledge_units.summary: To achieve a genuine externally rotated position for the front leg in the 90/90 hip switch, focus on two specific points of contact: the outside hip bone (greater trochanter) and the outside knee. Both points should be in contact with the ground.
execution_steps: Ensure the outside hip bone (greater trochanter) of the front leg is in contact with the ground.
Ensure the outside knee of the front leg is in contact with the ground.
cues: Find two points of contact: outside hip bone (greater trochanter) and outside knee.
errors_to_avoid: Pinching or discomfort in your hips.
Turning your spine to help find these points.

knowledge_units.title: Static 90/90 Position for Hip Mobility Restoration
knowledge_units.summary: For some individuals, simply holding the correct 90/90 position, ensuring all four specified points of contact (inside knee/ankle for back leg, outside hip/knee for front leg) are maintained, with hands flat on the ground and focusing on breathing, can be sufficient to restore hip mobility and produce meaningful change.
execution_steps: Sit in the 90/90 position, finding the most comfortable angle where all four points of contact can be maintained.
Ensure the outside hip and outside knee of the front leg are in contact with the ground.
Ensure the inside knee and inside ankle of the back leg are in contact with the ground.
Place hands flat on the ground for support.
Breathe deeply and hold the position.
cues: No pinching or discomfort in your hips whatsoever.
You shouldn't have to turn your spine to help find those points.
when_useful: Those who compensate with their spine during hip rotation exercises.
retest: Observe for actual meaningful change in hip mobility and reduced compensation.

model_notes: The video effectively uses both animated anatomical models and live demonstrations to explain complex biomechanical concepts and provide actionable corrective advice for a common mobility exercise. The focus on specific points of contact and avoiding compensation is highly valuable.
